subject: Quantly — topology constraints, SLO alignment & next actions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@quantly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantly — topology constraints, SLO alignment & next actions

Hi Elena — thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap to make sure we’re aligned and to propose concrete next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- P1: p95 text-generation latency spikes during peak trading hours cause poor UX for analysts.
- P2: Budget sensitivity for steady-state inference cost; procurement requires ~12-month predictability.
- P3: Data residency / audit trail requirements for certain EU customers (need VPC + audit logs).

Agreed goals
- SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: ~150 requests/s with 20% headroom for burst to 500 req/s.
- Model profile: ~13B-class open model (quantized) with deterministic reranks for internal scoring.

High-level deployment topology we discussed
- Primary: Dedicated VPC deployment in us-west with reserved GPU pool for low-latency traffic.
- Secondary: Hosted fallback (Redwood API) for overflow and batch-heavy backfills.
- Cache: KV/prefix caching for conversational traces; target cache hit >= 60% for repeated prompts.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) You: confirm a 48-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) for sizing (format: CSV with timestamps, prompt length, tokens).
2) Us (Redwood): deliver a topology diagram + RPS spreadsheet with steady-state and burst sizing (attaching initial draft).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security and our infra engineers this week — propose Thu/Fri.

Attachments: quantly-rps.xlsx (RPS baseline + sizing assumptions)

If I missed anything important, say so — otherwise I’ll loop in our infra leads and propose meeting times.

Best,
Rachel Kim

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantly — topology constraints, SLO alignment & next actions

Elena — thanks for the clarifications. Looping in Karthik (Infra), Connor (Runtime), and Marissa (Solutions) to pick up technical sizing, security checklist, and procurement framing. See an initial technical addendum below and attached diagram.

Technical addendum (notes from our infra/runtime teams)
- Baseline assumptions: average prompt ~110 tokens in, ~120 tokens generated out (~230 tokens/request). Tokenization variance accounted for in the spreadsheet.
- Latency drivers: KV cache misses, model loading/quantization path, and GPU warmup for large contexts. To meet p95<=200ms we recommend:
  * Dedicated A10G or equivalent for steady-state 13B-quantized models with continuous batching disabled for latency-critical routes (or low max batch window ~8–12ms).
  * H100 reserved pool if you want headroom for longer contexts or multimodal signals.
- Batching strategy: use small, bounded batching (max batch size 8) for latency-sensitive endpoint; use aggressive batching for background scoring.
- KV cache sizing: assume 40% hit necessary to keep p95 budget; for your traffic profile we estimate 120GB of KV cache (hot key eviction policy).
- Fallbacks: configure automated fallback to a smaller 7B quantized variant for overloads > 80% of reserved capacity; route non-interactive requests to hosted batch workers.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing will be enabled; we’ll surface p50/p95/p99 and token distribution histograms.

Proposed immediate tests
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour synthetic run (we’ll replay anonymized sample you provide) to validate p95 and throughput numbers; output will include per-model latency histograms and KV hit behavior.
2) If initial run looks good, set a 2-week pilot with a 1:10 traffic shadow to confirm production behavior.

Attachments: topology-diagram.png (draft topology), quantly-rps.xlsx (revised assumptions)

Action items for Quantly
- Share anonymized 48-hour traffic extract (CSV).
- Confirm procurement contact and desired SLA points for Reserved capacity pricing.
- Security: list required compliance docs (SOC2, audit window) or confirm required encryption/KMS processes.

I’ll schedule a 45-minute deep-dive for Thu 11:00–11:45 PT unless you propose something else.

Thanks — Rachel
